title: Trace, metrics, and dashboard coverage gap remediation after capacity regression
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a capacity regression incident on 2026-03-08 we discovered multiple blind spots in Console observability that delayed root cause identification and remediation. This ticket consolidates post-incident findings into a prioritized action plan to expand metric coverage, improve dashboard fidelity, and add targeted traces for autoscaling and model-fallback flows. The goal is to reduce mean time to detect and mean time to mitigate for similar capacity/regression events.
incident_summary: On 2026-03-08 a batch of serving nodes experienced higher-than-expected token queuing and fell back from a preferred quantized model variant to a CPU fallback. Customers observed latency spikes and higher per-token cost. Initial detection was via customer reports; internal dashboards did not surface the problem quickly because key signals were either absent or aggregated away.
timeline_summary: 2026-03-08 03:20 UTC — First customer report of sustained latency > 1s on generation endpoints.
2026-03-08 03:25 UTC — Ops paging triggered by error-rate alert (false negative for capacity pressure).
2026-03-08 03:40 UTC — On-call investigated host metrics; host-level CPU and GPU metrics looked nominal due to averaging across pools.
2026-03-08 04:05 UTC — Manual trace sampling found KV cache eviction spikes and repeated model fallback events for a small subset of routes.
2026-03-08 04:30 UTC — Rollback of recent autoscaler change mitigated fallbacks; full mitigation by 05:10 UTC.
2026-03-09 — Post-incident review began; discovered multiple missing signals and dashboard design issues that obscured the failure mode.
root_causes: Missing per-route model-variant metrics: dashboards only showed cluster-wide model counts; no metric captured fallback_rate or model_variant_switches per route.
Aggregated percentile masking: Console dashboards displayed p95 across heterogeneous routes, masking single-route regressions with high latency.
Trace sampling excluded autoscaler control-plane operations and KV cache lifecycle events (evictions/insertions), so key sequencing was absent from traces.
No alert for sustained prefix KV cache miss ratio > 10% combined with rising input queue depth; existing alerts were on CPU/GPU utilization only.
Dashboard queries relied on 5m rollups; transient spikes that triggered fallbacks were lost in rollups.
impact: Customer-facing latency spikes and increased cost due to CPU fallbacks for affected routes.
Longer time-to-detect (approx. 45 minutes) and longer time-to-mitigate (approx. 110 minutes) compared to our target SLOs for incident handling.
Operational overhead: manual tracing and ad-hoc log correlation required to confirm KV cache eviction pattern and autoscaler misbehavior.
action_items: Add per-route metrics: instrument fallback_rate, model_variant_in_use, kv_cache_hit_ratio, and queue_depth at request-route granularity. Owner: @l.oconnor. Estimate: 3 points.
Create high-cardinality dashboards: replace single-aggregate p95 panels with route-scoped p50/p95/p99 views and route filters. Owner: @observability-team. Estimate: 2 points.

Increase trace coverage: include autoscaler control-plane events and KV cache lifecycle events in request traces; enable dynamic sampling for routes with >0.5% fallback_rate. Owner: @m.chen and @infra-tracing. Estimate: 3 points.
New alerts: add composite alert that fires when (queue_depth > threshold AND kv_cache_miss_ratio > 0.1) for 2 consecutive minutes, with runbook link. Owner: @s.reyes. Estimate: 2 points.
Reduce dashboard rollup intervals for critical panels to 30s with an option to expand to 5m for long-term retention. Owner: @console-ui. Estimate: 1 point.

Add synthetic test job: nightly synthetic workload that validates per-route latency and fallback_rate against baseline; surface regressions to Slack channel #rt-observability. Owner: @qa. Estimate: 2 points.
Document and update runbooks: add explicit steps for diagnosing model fallback and KV cache eviction patterns, include query snippets and trace anchors. Owner: @oncall-leads. Estimate: 1 point.
Post-deploy verification checklist: verify new metrics are visible in dashboards and alerts trigger during staged fault-injection. Owner: @release. Estimate: 1 point.
